name: narrow_eq_tcga
note: Narrow equality on a TCGA attribute (A.ALN is 91,242 TCGA of 91,356). EXACT is advanced_search's rule: case-insensitive equality with the trimmed MSIStatus value, so 'MSI' and 'msi' match alike; an extensions.where on the same value would be exact and case-sensitive. The term also occurs inside the key names MSIScore and MSIStatus, so advanced_search's SQL stage reads 25,226 A.ALN rows before its Python stage keeps the matches. MySQL: 758.

name: narrow_eq_production
note: Narrow equality on a production attribute (MUS has no TCGA samples). EXACT: case-insensitive equality with the trimmed Genotype value; an extensions.where would be exact and case-sensitive. 583 MUS rows contain the text anywhere in their JSON. MySQL: 427.

name: type_only_near_100k
note: Broad type-only: every TIS sample, production and TCGA mixed, so each scope sees a different share. No text term, so no matching rule applies. Over 50,000 rows: parity's A side is the id-only SQL form. MySQL: 107,412 (33,939 TCGA, 73,473 production).

name: type_only_avcf
note: Broad type-only: A.VCF, the largest type. No text term, so no matching rule applies. Over 50,000 rows: parity's A side is the id-only SQL form. MySQL: 283,311 (283,302 TCGA, 9 production).

name: crossed_attributes
note: Crossed attributes: 'lung' must be a case-insensitive substring of both Organ and SiteOfResection (attribute_logic AND). PARTIAL folds case, so Organ values 'Lung', 'LUNG' and 'Bronchus and lung' all count; an exact, case-sensitive where on Organ = 'Lung' would take only the first spelling. advanced_search's SQL stage reads 26,503 TIS rows that contain the text. MySQL: 2,488.

name: keyword_all_types
note: Keyword across every sample type, one of the two breaking shapes. Case-insensitive substring of any value ('Granuloma' and 'granuloma' alike); key names do not count. advanced_search's SQL stage matches 5,385 rows, 704 of which hold the text only outside a value (a key name such as NewGranulomaCount), and its Python stage drops those. MySQL: 4,681 by the value rule (0 TCGA).

name: or_retry_three_terms
note: Nessie's OR retry exactly as sent, the other breaking shape: _advanced_search_retry_attempts (NessieAI/chat_nextseek/src/chat_nextseek/helpers/tools/nextseek_api.py) joins the retry terms with ' OR ' into one string. advanced_search's PubMed parser takes one operator per level, so it rejects three operands, scans every sample with a LIKE on the whole string and keeps a row only when one value contains all of it; graph_search keeps the string as one term (declared difference 2). Both answer 0 here. Changed from the list ['granuloma', 'tuberculosis', 'macaque'] by E6: the view nests a list of three or more terms as (granuloma) OR ((tuberculosis) OR (macaque)), and seek/search.py's designSearchPubmed raises IndexError on any such nesting, so advanced_search answers 502 to the list in every scope (graph_search: 7,480), and a shape one side cannot answer cannot prove parity. MySQL: 0.

name: multi_type_text
note: Several types plus a term, crossing production (CEL) and TCGA (most PAT and PAV). Case-insensitive substring of any value, so 'Malignant melanoma, NOS' and 'Melanoma' both match. MySQL: 2,923 (2,843 TCGA, 80 production).

name: uids_50
note: 50 UIDs, 25 TCGA then 25 production, the first by CRC32(id) order among uuids that match UID_RE and are not duplicated (production ones also belong to a project). Every term is a UID, so both engines take the uuid path: exact, byte-for-byte, no case folding. MySQL: 50.

name: query_not
note: The Advanced box's NOT. advanced_search gets the text in filter_searchText and parses it (a NOT b is LIKE a AND NOT LIKE b over the JSON text, then any term in a value); graph_search gets it in extensions.query. Declared difference 2 does not apply: the two forms must give the same rows.

name: query_grouped_or
note: AND and OR mixed through the parentheses the Add button writes, one operator per level.

name: query_tagged_not
note: A term[TYPE] tag limits its term to the sample type; the NOT applies across every type.

name: query_not_key_name
note: A negated term that is a key name: advanced_search's NOT LIKE drops every sample whose type has an Organ attribute, which graph_search reads from the catalog.

name: query_exact_or
note: EXACT through the query text: a term equal to a value, case-insensitive; stage 1 stays a substring.

name: filtering_not_contain
note: The Simple box's Not Contain: advanced_search's own FILTERING path (/seek/samples/searching/) against the where operator NOT CONTAINS. Case-sensitive, over samples that hold Organ.

name: filtering_contain
note: The Simple box's Contain through the same path, now that CONTAINS reads the value's text. True and False have no fixture here: the Simple box offers them for attribute type 15, and no attribute has that type in production (scripts/graph_search/synthetic_queries.json has them).

name: where_paired
note: Paired where on one type, ANDed, exact and case-sensitive: TCGA's spellings 'female' and 'asian' match, and production spellings such as 'Female', 'F' or 'White' are not folded in (advanced_search's EXACT would fold case). MySQL: 308 by byte-exact comparison (all TCGA).

name: where_numeric_range
note: Numeric range on a SEEK Float attribute. RIN is text in json_metadata and a float on the node, so the range compares numbers and sees only values that cast (G6's census has 0 RIN cast failures). No case question. MySQL: 9,168 RNA samples whose RIN parses as a number in [7, 9) (9,092 TCGA, 76 production).

name: lineage_descendant
note: Lineage: TIS samples with a D.SEQ sample within 4 DERIVED_FROM hops below them (D.SEQ's parents are DNA samples). No text term, so no matching rule applies. MySQL: 5,729 (all production), counted by walking the declared parent tokens (graph_sync.sources.declared_lineage) up 4 hops from all 6,705 D.SEQ samples. A path through an OrphanSample node exists only in the graph.
